analysis.title: GS Sharkey - US Equities Mid Day Color 6 Nov 2026
key_insights: Equities reverted higher on Nov 6 (NDX > RTY > SPX) after a whipsaw week. SPX is just above its 200-day moving average and over 60% of its constituents are down on the day.
October NFP printed 165k vs 70k expected. VIX is 'normalizing' to a 25-handle after its largest 1-day change since Covid. WTI is down slightly, below $90.

NDX rose 1.3% after its worst day since 3/9/20. The GS high beta momentum index (GSPRHIMO) rose 2.4% after closing down 6.2% on Nov 5, and is down 51% from its June highs. SOX rose 3% after its worst day since 2020 and closed 14% below its 200-day moving average.
GS TMT flow shows a lack of conviction and muted activity. Flows are more balanced than Nov 5, with some dip buying in smaller notional size.

Global Fundamental L/S hedge funds were down 1.3% on Nov 5 (a -2 standard deviation move), driven by beta exposure. GS Prime shows more hedging through Macro Products, with no sign of panic or accelerated degrossing. 7 of 11 sectors were net sold, led by info tech, consumer discretionary and industrials.
SPX top-of-book liquidity averaged $4mm on Nov 5, one of the least liquid sessions in four years, and was $3mm on Nov 6. ETFs were 35% of the tape (32% on Nov 5, 28% YTD average).
GS says CTAs are significant sellers of SPX and NDX over the next week: a combined $30mn in a flat tape, $22.3mn in an up tape and $31.2mm in a down tape.

GS franchise activity is 5 out of 10 with flows skewed 6.6% better to buy. Long-only clients are skewed 7.6% better to buy (communication services, industrials, info tech). Hedge funds are skewed 7.8% better to buy (macro products, info tech, energy). Info tech demand is on track to break a 6-day sell streak.
ETFs had their third-largest notional volume day in the GS dataset on Nov 5, at $580bn and 33% of the tape. Levered ETFs took in a record $3bn and inverse ETFs saw a record $2bn of outflows.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The print beat expectations by a wide margin. Equities still reverted higher in a volatile week.
VIX is normalizing after its largest 1-day change since Covid.

Lack of conviction in TMT flows and dip buying in smaller size.
